title: Balancing IA Deadlines and University Applications
summary: Learn a practical DP2 plan for balancing IA deadlines with university applications from September to November while protecting grades and sleep.
body_markdown:
Balancing IA deadlines with university applications requires one integrated calendar, concrete weekly priorities, and protected time for both commitments. During the **IB DP2 fall term** , work backwards from confirmed deadlines, complete high-risk IA stages early, and avoid leaving applications for whatever time remains.


September to November can combine school-set IA deadlines, predicted grades, references, admissions tests, essays, and normal IB lessons. The aim is not to advance everything equally, but to sequence tasks before they become emergencies.


### Confirm the deadlines that apply to you


There is no universal student IA deadline across all IB schools. Teachers mark internal assessment before the IB moderates the school's marking, but **your school sets the deadline you must follow** . This gives teachers time for feedback where permitted, authentication, marking, standardisation, and submission.


Ask each teacher or your DP coordinator to confirm:


- Proposal, data collection, draft, and final dates
- Which dates are checkpoints and which are final submissions
- When permitted teacher feedback will be returned
- Which work may contribute to predicted grades
- The school's late-submission policy


The[IB assessment overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/) explains the role of internal assessment, while RevisionDojo's guide to[when IAs are due](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/when-are-ias-due) clarifies the difference between school deadlines and IB procedures.


Application dates also vary. For **2027 UK entry** , UCAS lists **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, and veterinary courses. Most other undergraduate courses have an equal consideration deadline of **13 January 2027** , although schools commonly set earlier internal dates.


US institutions choose their own deadlines, with many early rounds falling near the beginning of November. The University of California's fall 2027 filing period runs from **1 October-30 November 2026** . Check programme, scholarship, portfolio, testing, and financial aid dates separately.


### Build one master deadline map


Using separate planners for IAs and applications hides collisions. Put every requirement into one calendar and label it **fixed** , **school-controlled** , or **self-imposed** .


Deadline type Examples Response


Fixed external UCAS, university portal, admissions test Finish several days early


School-controlled IA draft, reference request, predicted grade review Confirm with the relevant staff member


Self-imposed Essay outline, data analysis, proofreading Schedule early enough to create a buffer


Include transcripts, references, fees, portfolios, and additional questionnaires. Set a personal submission target **3-7 days** before an external deadline, while giving counselors and teachers substantially more notice.


Break each IA into visible outputs. Replace “work on Biology IA” with “clean raw data,” “calculate uncertainties,” or “draft the evaluation.” The[IA time-management guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/time-management-strategies-for-completing-your-ia-on-schedule) explains how milestones make progress easier to measure.


### Follow a September-to-November plan


The exact sequence depends on your school and destination, but this framework suits many May-session DP2 students.


Period IA priority Application priority


September Confirm dates, stabilise research questions, and complete data or source collection Finalise choices, request references, organise records, and outline responses


Early October Produce analysis and complete approaching drafts Finish early UK applications, tests, and portfolios


Late October Apply permitted feedback and conduct final checks Complete early US essays, forms, and counselor requirements


November Submit due IAs and begin the next milestone Complete November applications early and prepare later submissions


Use September to remove uncertainty. An unstable question, method, dataset, or source base deserves attention before extensive application polishing because research problems become harder to repair later.


October is usually the main production period. Early UK applicants may prioritise their application during the opening weeks, while students facing November US deadlines should draft their main essay before late October. RevisionDojo's[global university application guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-apply-to-university-as-an-ib-student-step-by-step-guide-for-global-admissions) outlines the documents used by different systems.


In November, reserve separate sessions for writing, portal administration, and IA checks. Submitting applications early reduces the risk that a technical problem consumes coursework time.


### Plan each week in two lanes


Create an **IA lane** and an **application lane** so that the louder task does not absorb every available hour. A demanding week might include:


- Three **60-90 minute IA blocks**
- Two **45-60 minute application blocks**
- One administrative session for portals and documents
- Three short subject-revision sessions
- One weekly planning review


This is a planning model, not an IB requirement. Give every session a specific output, such as “draft two analysis paragraphs,” rather than “do coursework.” Schedule reasoning and essay writing during high-focus periods, leaving citations, file organisation, and portal checks for lower-energy times. The[two-lane approach to IB and applications](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-do-i-help-my-teen-balance-ib-and-university-applications) offers a related model.


### Resolve deadline collisions logically


When deadlines clash, compare **urgency, consequence, dependency, remaining work, and recovery options** . A fixed application deadline normally outranks a self-imposed IA target, while a final school IA deadline outranks optional application polishing.


Consider whether someone else is waiting for your work. A counselor may need your information before an external deadline, while an unresolved IA method may prevent all later analysis. If the order remains unclear, ask your teacher or counselor what must be completed first rather than assuming an extension is available.


### Protect predicted grades, revision, and sleep


Applications do not replace normal academic responsibilities. Schools may use tests, classwork, coursework progress, mock examinations, and teacher judgment when producing predicted grades. Ask what evidence remains relevant instead of assuming one IA will determine your prediction.


Maintain short revision sessions during application-heavy weeks. Flashcards, a focused Questionbank set, or one timed response can preserve recall and exam technique. A[balanced IB study schedule](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-create-a-balanced-ib-study-schedule) can help fit these habits around coursework.


Keep a consistent stopping time. Late-night work often leads to weak analysis, inaccurate application details, and slower work the next day.


### Avoid common DP2 planning mistakes


Do not treat draft and final deadlines as interchangeable. A draft allows permitted feedback to influence the work, but students should not expect unlimited teacher editing or assume that a final submission can be reopened.


Avoid perfecting one task while another remains structurally incomplete. Prioritise accurate information, sound reasoning, evidence, and analysis before formatting or minor stylistic changes.


Enter portal details early and confirm that recommenders know their deadlines. Common App states that its displayed submission deadline is generally **11:59 pm in the applicant's local time zone** , but submitting earlier leaves time to resolve problems.


Your IA and application writing must remain your own. AI may help explain a criterion or organise a checklist, but it should not invent assessed reasoning or personal experiences. Follow school academic integrity rules and disclose AI use when required.


### Use a weekly final check


Every Sunday, identify the next external deadline, the next school IA deadline, one required IA output, one application output, any person waiting for information, and the location of your submission buffer. If an answer is unclear, resolving it becomes the first task.


### Conclusion


Balancing IA deadlines and university applications is mainly a sequencing problem. Confirm dates, combine them in one calendar, work through specific milestones, and protect time for revision and sleep. RevisionDojo's Coursework Review, Jojo AI, Questionbank, and Flashcards can reduce friction while your planning, reasoning, and submitted work remain your own.
